evidence.note: Opens by reading the template (cat train_AGENT_template.py), listing the data shards and tokenizer dir, and confirming torch/sentencepiece availability — orients to template, data format, and tokenizer before editing.

Derives the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope up front: '32MB / 1 byte per param ≈ 32M params; with int8+zlib can fit ~30M' and computes per-layer param counts to pick dims — turning the byte cap into a concrete architecture constraint.

Before full training, sanity-checks param count and save/reload int8 round-trip, finds ckpt 42.7MB too big, and iterates configs (512/8/3, 512/9/3, 512/10/2.5) against the cap — actively probing the size/quantization design space.

Reads the .bin file to confirm format (137M tokens, uint16 = 2 bytes/token) rather than assuming; separately reverse-engineers the grader's bpb metric (bits-per-byte vs per-token) and derives the 0.3729 conversion factor to interpret the target correctly.

Final verification maps the full forward/load contract: returns (args, model) tuple, logits (B,T,V) float32, position-dependent (pos 0 vs 512), loss equals manual cross_entropy; confirms ckpt 31,743,016 < 32,000,000 (decimal MB) and implements both load paths (load_model_for_verification AND GPT class + dequantize_state_dict_int8).

reasoning: The agent deliberately mapped the full contract — probing actual data (uint16 bin), tokenizer, both load paths, the (args,model) tuple form, position-dependence, and loss==cross_entropy — matching the level-8 anchor, and additionally derived the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope up front and checked the decimal byte cap, which are level-10 behaviors. It falls short of a full 10 only in not explicitly engineering for bf16-noise stability, placing it at a strong 9.
